content:
Phase 34 implementation submitted (branch phase-34-arbiter-cockpit, commit 7c85291; pytest 861 passed / 5 skipped; version 0.11.0). Plan: docs/phases/arbiter-cockpit-30-arc.md (approved r3). Findings incl. the browser dogfood: docs/phases/arbiter-cockpit-findings.md.

What was built, in the plan's order:
0. `cycle.compute_scope_diff(phase, type, project_dir)` extracted; `_cli_scope_diff` is a thin caller; `ScopeDiffError` carries the exact CLI messages; test asserts byte-identical stdout.
1. `tagteam/server.py`: `TagteamHTTPServer(ThreadingHTTPServer)` in both modes; `make_handler(project_dir, mode=legacy|cockpit, token, max_sse, ...)`; `resolve_serve_options` (`--theme saloon|cockpit`, `--host`, `--max-sse`, `serve.theme` config gate); legacy = 0.10.0-identical (Saloon at `/`, bind "", four legacy POSTs without token, `*` CORS, no meta, new endpoints 404 — regression-tested); cockpit = loopback default, per-run 32-byte token as `<meta name="tagteam-token">` required as `X-Tagteam-Token` on EVERY POST incl. the legacy four, Origin/Referer must match `Host`, no `*` CORS on any response (note: dropped on cockpit GETs too — a wildcard on the token-bearing page would leak the token; see findings), `Cache-Control: no-store` on the page.
2. `tagteam/cockpit_api.py` (new, pure): now/rounds(+interjections)/interjections/briefs/brief/brief-current (same rule as `tagteam brief`)/usage (aggregate + by_agent + per-turn series + rate_limits w/ resets_in_s)/scope-diff (per-file `files:[{path,status,binary,additions,deletions,patch,truncated,bytes}]`, ≤200 KB / ≤400 files, flags)/tail (same resolution as `tagteam tail --no-follow`)/events_signature + signature_id.
3. SSE `GET /api/events`: 1 s sampler (state seq, rounds file size+mtime, max ids of interjections/briefs/usage/rate_limits, briefs status digest, delivered/retired counts, pause marker, inflight stem/pid), `id:`+`event: change`+`data:`, heartbeat every 15 s, Last-Event-ID → snapshot, `--max-sse` cap → 503 JSON, per-tick peer-close detection so a closed tab frees its slot within one interval; per-connection threads; server `stop_event`.
4. Action endpoints `/api/pause|resume|interject|interject/retire|cancel-turn|brief/generate|rule` → thin wrappers over `controls.*_command` / `briefer.brief_command` with captured `out`: `{ok, message, rc, cli}`, `by = web:<user>`, `{"dry_run": true}` returns the exact CLI line (used by confirmations), 400 for bad params, 409 for CLI refusals (e.g. rule on a non-escalated cycle → `{ok:false}`), 500 JSON never a traceback.
5. Schema v6 `rate_limits(provider, kind unique; status, resets_at ISO, payload_json, ts)` + `upsert_rate_limit`/`latest_rate_limits`; `headless.parse_rate_limits`/`record_rate_limits` (latest per kind from Claude's `rate_limit_event.rate_limit_info`; Codex → none) wired after usage recording in the engine and briefer; in `NON_FILE_BACKED_TABLES` (repair test); v5→v6 additive migration test; 0.10.0 verified to open a v6 DB in a scratch venv.
6. Frontend `cockpit.html|css|js` (plain JS): Now strip → Needs you (typed cards: escalation w/ brief sections + Approve/Request changes, question + Answer w/ `to`, hold + Resume, missing/failed brief + Generate brief, stale in-flight / no watcher, no-tagteam.yaml) → Watch tabs (Feed newest-first with type chips + expanders; Diff file list first, per-file expand, truncation banners; Usage rate-limit line + churn SVG with r10 line + role/cycle/process tables; Notes with Interject/Retire); feedback contract (pending spinner → toast with server message + CLI; ok:false inline; Live/Polling/Disconnected indicator; SSE change → targeted re-fetch); confirmations show the CLI with content; Approve/Cancel turn separated; teaching empty states; `?theme=saloon` link. Saloon `app.js`: `tagteamFetch()` (token header only when the meta exists) + a Cockpit link in cockpit mode only.
7. Docs: README "The Cockpit" (+ Saloon as theme, security note), roadmap, findings, SKILL.md one-line mention (both copies), CLI help; version 0.11.0.

Tests: tests/test_cockpit_api.py (25), tests/test_server_cockpit.py (25 — both modes on a real ephemeral-port server: legacy identity incl. verbatim index.html and 404s, pages/assets/meta, token+origin on all POSTs incl. the legacy four both ways, reads, writes, SSE two clients/heartbeat/Last-Event-ID/cap 503/non-blocking, flags + config gate), test_db v6 (3), test_headless rate-limit capture (3, incl. the recorded real fixture), test_briefer repair preservation of rate_limits; the fake agent now emits the rate-limit frame.

Deviations noted for you: (a) `*` CORS dropped on all cockpit-mode responses, not only POST (token leak otherwise); (b) `--no-open` listed as "existing" in the plan never existed — not added; (c) legacy `/api/rounds` unchanged, `interjections` attached only in cockpit mode; (d) `?nosse=1` debug switch to force the polling path. Browser dogfood recorded in the findings (ruling from the browser on the scratch escalation, pause/resume as the hold on this repo, Usage over 26 real rows, two-tab SSE via a CLI pause, polling fallback, tail drawer); the "Feed live during a headless reviewer turn" item will be observed during this impl cycle and amended into the findings. No arbiter interjections were pending.

The implementation is substantial and the valid project environment is green (`.venv/bin/pytest -q`: 861 passed, 5 skipped; targeted cockpit/schema/headless/repair tests: 57 passed). I found two blocking behavioral gaps that the current tests do not cover:

1. Watcher liveness is false for Tagteam's own normal launch shape. This repo currently has PID 74337 running `/Users/jackblacketter/projects/tagteam/.venv/bin/python -m tagteam watch --mode iterm2`, but `_get_watcher_status('/Users/jackblacketter/projects/tagteam')` and `now_payload(...)["watcher"]` both return `{running: false, pid: null}`. `_get_watcher_status` requires the project path in argv, while `session._watcher_command()` starts the watcher from the project cwd without putting that path in argv. Consequently the persistent Now strip reports `no watcher` for a live watcher and can generate incorrect guidance. Implement a reliable project-bound liveness signal for the launch modes Tagteam itself creates (with PID identity/stale-record handling as appropriate), and add a test for a watcher whose cwd is the project but whose argv contains no project path.

2. `/api/scope-diff` is not per-file for untracked directories, which are a common new-phase shape. In a clean temp repo, after cycle init and creating `newpkg/a.py` plus `newpkg/b.py`, `compute_scope_diff` returns `['.tagteam/', 'docs/', 'newpkg/']`; `scope_diff_payload` emits those three directory entries with `additions: null` and no patch. Thus the cockpit cannot show either source file, and it also surfaces Tagteam's own `.tagteam/` and collapsed `docs/` bookkeeping directories. Preserve the required byte-identical CLI output, but make the cockpit payload expand attributable untracked directories into actual file entries, filter Tagteam artifacts at file level, and return real patches/counts/statuses. Add coverage for an untracked directory with multiple text files plus collapsed Tagteam directories; also assert accurate added/deleted/binary status rather than treating every tracked existing path as `modified`.

Before resubmission, finish the still-open findings item for a live reviewer turn after these fixes. Also reconcile the claim that cockpit mode has no wildcard CORS on any response with `server.py`'s unconditional `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on static assets (either remove it in cockpit mode or narrow the documentation; the token-bearing HTML and all POST responses must remain non-wildcard). No arbiter interjections were present.

Round 2 (commit on phase-34-arbiter-cockpit; pytest 869 passed / 5 skipped). All four r1 items addressed; details in docs/phases/arbiter-cockpit-findings.md ("Deviations" + "Live headless turn (round 2)").

1. Watcher liveness, project-bound. (a) `watch()` now writes `.tagteam/watcher.json` {pid, creation identity, mode, argv, project_dir} for its lifetime and removes it in `finally` (tests: written during the loop, removed on return and on exception). (b) New `cockpit_api.watcher_status(project_dir, inflight)` → `{running, pid, mode, source, stale_pidfile}` with three signals in order: the pidfile (dead pid or identity mismatch → `stale_pidfile: true`, never trusted), a process scan of `tagteam … watch` processes whose argv names the project OR whose cwd is the project (new `procs.cwd`: /proc on Linux, `lsof -a -p PID -d cwd -Fn` on macOS — this catches pre-pidfile watchers such as this repo's live pid 74337: verified `{running: True, pid: 74337, mode: 'iterm2', source: 'process-scan'}`), and the in-flight pointer's watcher identity. `now_payload` uses it; the strip shows `watcher <mode> pid N` / `watcher gone (stale record)`. Tests: pidfile running / dead-pid stale / identity-mismatch stale; a real `… tagteam watch --mode iterm2` sleeper started from the project cwd with no project path on argv is detected, the same shape started elsewhere is not (gated `needs_proc_inspection` for your sandbox); `now_payload` surfaces it. The legacy `/api/watcher/status` helper is deliberately unchanged (flag-off identity) — the cockpit no longer uses it.

2. `/api/scope-diff` per file. CLI output unchanged (test still asserts `['.tagteam/', 'docs/', 'newpkg/']`-style collapsed dirs byte-identical). The payload now expands collapsed untracked directories via `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` into files, filters Tagteam bookkeeping at FILE level (CLI artifact set + `.tagteam/`), and reports real per-file additions/deletions/patch with accurate statuses: `untracked`, `added` (tracked, absent from the baseline tree via `git ls-tree` on the baseline), `modified`, `deleted` (unstaged or staged), `binary`. Returns both `paths` (CLI list) and `file_paths` (expanded). Tests: a new package with two text files + a binary alongside collapsed `.tagteam/` and `docs/` (no .gitignore) → `file_paths == ['docs/phases/feat-x.md', 'newpkg/a.py', 'newpkg/b.py', 'newpkg/img.bin']`, no `.tagteam/`/`docs/handoffs/` entries, real counts/patches; an added/modified/deleted(unstaged and staged)/binary matrix.

3. CORS: static assets no longer send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` in cockpit mode (`_cors()` everywhere); tests assert no wildcard on `/`, `/cockpit.css|js`, JSON reads and 404s in cockpit mode, and `*` on `/` and `/app.js` in legacy mode. Findings wording now matches: no wildcard on ANY cockpit-mode response.

4. Findings item — live headless turn — recorded with a REAL headless turn on the scratch project (this repo's impl reviews are dispatched by Jack's iterm2 watcher to an interactive Codex, and a second watcher would double-dispatch): strip `in flight: Claude (lead) · 29s` + `watcher headless pid 20552` (pidfile) + Tail drawer streaming the real `claude -p` session with `Cancel turn` in the drawer; turn ok in 59 s → Feed gained the r2 entry live; Usage shows the first REAL rate-limit row (`claude five hour window: allowed, resets 10:20 PM (in 3h30m)`) and the churn point. Then the watcher was killed mid-turn: strip `process gone` / `watcher gone (stale record)`, attention card → `Cancel turn` from the browser removed the stale pointer (CLI's own message in the toast). That dogfood exposed one more gap, fixed here: the SSE signature had no process-liveness signal, so a dying watcher/turn never fired a frame — the signature now includes `inflight.alive` and `watcher {pid, alive}` (tests), and the page adds a 30 s safety refresh in live mode.

No arbiter interjections were pending.

The round-1 functional issues are fixed and verified: the live pre-pidfile watcher is now detected by project cwd; the exact untracked-directory reproduction expands to real file entries with patches/counts while preserving the collapsed CLI paths; cockpit CORS is consistent; the focused suite passes 72 tests and the full suite passes 869 with 5 skipped. The completed headless-turn dogfood is also sufficient.

One blocking compatibility issue remains. `watch()` now calls `write_pidfile(pidfile_root, mode)` unconditionally, so a bare `tagteam watch` on a project with no cockpit flag and no `serve.theme: cockpit` writes `.tagteam/watcher.json` for the process lifetime. That is new flag-off behavior outside the cockpit server. It conflicts with proposal §2's inherited hard requirement (new behavior must be opt-in; flags off behaves identically to the previous release) and this approved plan's explicit standing criterion that `ThreadingHTTPServer` is the only shared change. Keeping the legacy `/api/watcher/status` route unchanged does not restore that process/filesystem contract.

Gate the persistent watcher record behind a cockpit opt-in (the existing config gate, an explicit watcher option, a cockpit-server-owned activation marker, or another design that preserves reliable cockpit liveness) while retaining the cwd-bound process scan/inflight fallback as appropriate. Add a regression test proving ordinary flag-off `watch()` creates no new watcher file or other persistent behavior, alongside the opt-in lifecycle and stale-identity tests. Update the findings to state how CLI-only `serve --theme cockpit` and config-enabled cockpit obtain liveness without weakening the flag-off guarantee.

No arbiter interjections were present.

Round 3 (commit on phase-34-arbiter-cockpit; pytest 871 passed / 5 skipped). The one r2 item — the watcher pidfile was unconditional, i.e. new flag-off behavior — is fixed:

- `watch()` now keeps `.tagteam/watcher.json` ONLY when the project has opted into the cockpit: `serve: {theme: cockpit}` in tagteam.yaml (the existing config gate; `watcher.pidfile_enabled()` reads it) or the new explicit `tagteam watch --pidfile` (parsed by `watch_command`, passed as `pidfile=True`; `pidfile=False` forces it off even with the config gate). Bare `tagteam watch` writes nothing new — regression test `test_flag_off_watch_creates_no_new_files` snapshots the project tree before / during the loop / after and asserts identical trees and that no `.tagteam/` is even created; the opt-in lifecycle (config gate: written during, removed on return and on exception) and the explicit-flag override tests sit alongside; the stale-identity tests in test_cockpit_api are unchanged.
- Liveness without the pidfile is preserved: `watcher_status()` still falls back to the cwd-bound process scan (finds every launch shape Tagteam itself creates — session backends start the watcher from the project cwd — plus any argv naming the project; verified again on this repo's live pid 74337) and to the in-flight runner identity during headless turns.
- Findings ("Watcher liveness" deviation) and README now state how each activation gets liveness: CLI-only `serve --theme cockpit` → no pidfile, cwd scan + inflight (add `--pidfile` for the identity-checked record); config-enabled cockpit → the watcher keeps the pidfile automatically (same gate that switches the server), scan/inflight remain the fallback. `ThreadingHTTPServer` is again the only change shared with flag-off runs.

No arbiter interjections were pending.
